notes: voice.cpp is too entangled. So run.sh cuts the unchanged part out of voice.cpp (from the renderWave instance to the end of Voice::renderOsc). The Voice mock in stubs/osc_shim.h contains only the members that renderOsc needs. So the benchmark runs real firmware code with real tables. It measures exactly what renderBasicSource calls per unison part (mono, applyAmplitude=true, 4 blocks warm-up, 10 blocks counted). The wavetable oscillator is not included, because its setup needs a sample, clusters and the FFT. The pan loop for stereo unison in renderBasicSource (memset and scalar 2x smmul per sample and part) is not measured. I estimate it at ~1300 per part; with NEON (vmull/vshrn) it could also be done bit-exactly. On the PC it needs -m32 and a scalar NEON replacement (stubs_pc). The checksums match ARM, except for crude, the triangle <~711 Hz and saw PW: the PC fallbacks of the *_rounded functions in fixedpoint.h truncate instead of rounding. So always compare bit-exactness ARM against ARM. In context: an oscillator without unison costs ~0.13% per voice. It only becomes relevant with unison (8 parts: 1.1% per oscillator and voice).
